rv.q: Yet, for all the on-stage energy, for all the good wheezes in the script...it has a fatal lack of tension.
That said, this is largely a joyous show.
It should leave you wanting more; this left me wanting a bit less.
This comedy has, of course, actually done everything right.

Perhaps not in name, but with its highly physical comedy, send-ups of familiar tropes (here posh chaps in cricket jumpers and blazers, overwrought music cues and overcomplicated denouements), Mark Bell’s production provides a similar chaotic joy.
Mischief have made themselves the pre-eminent force in farce in theatre today
With the Peter Pan Goes Wrong tour coming to the West End soon, and That Goes Wrong run looking unstoppable, Mischief have turned disaster into triumph.
